notes.meaning: Michael, the great angelic protector, will stand up to defend God's people during a time of terrible crisis. This hardship will be more severe than any trouble the world has ever seen. Even so, God promises that everyone whose name is recorded in his book of life will be completely delivered.

differ.view: This points forward to a future Great Tribulation, where Jewish people whose names are written in God's book will be preserved before Christ returns.
Michael represents Christ guarding his elect church, promising that all true spiritual believers will be preserved through the severe trials of history.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: This was fulfilled when Michael defended the Jews under the Maccabees, but it also points to his protection of the Church against the Antichrist.

notes.meaning: People who have died and returned to the dust will physically wake up from the sleep of death. The faithful will rise to enjoy everlasting life with God, while the ungodly will awake to everlasting disgrace and punishment. This passage offers the Old Testament's clearest promise of bodily resurrection for both the just and the unjust.

Those who remain wise in God's truth and lead others into his righteousness will receive dazzling heavenly honor. They will shine with lasting splendor like the bright sky and the stars above. God deeply values those who do not keep their faith to themselves but help guide others to salvation.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Christian teachers, martyrs, and those who practice virginity receive an extra crown of heavenly glory beyond the basic joy shared by all the saved.

notes.meaning: Daniel is commanded to preserve these prophetic words safely, like an unalterable treasure, until the time of the end. As that final period approaches, people will search the Scriptures thoroughly, and true knowledge of God's plan will grow. The prophecy was sealed not to hide it forever, but to keep it secure until history proved it true.

differ.view: Running to and fro and the increase of knowledge describe modern travel, digital communication, and the explosion of end-times prophecy studies.

notes.meaning: Daniel looks up and sees two other heavenly messengers standing on opposite banks of the river Tigris. They appear as attendants around the Lord, ready to carry out his royal commands. Placing one on each bank confirms that God's word is fully witnessed and securely established.

One of the angels speaks to the majestic figure dressed in linen above the waters, asking how long these astonishing troubles will last. Even holy angels care deeply about God's people and desire to understand his secret timetable. Their question is recorded to stir us up to take God's promises just as seriously.

The heavenly man raises both hands toward heaven and swears by the living God that the trial is firmly fixed. The affliction will continue until the independent strength of God's holy people has been broken. Only when all human self-reliance is shattered will God step in to finish the trouble and deliver his people.

differ.view: The phrase a time, times, and half a time is not a strict calendar measurement, but a symbolic picture of a long season of trial that God cuts short for the sake of his people.
This phrase refers to a literal three and a half years of final tribulation before Christ returns.

notes.meaning: Daniel hears the angel's answer, but he admits that he cannot understand what it means. He respectfully asks what the final outcome of all these strange events will be. Even the greatest prophets had limits to their understanding and had to depend completely on God's timing.

The heavenly messenger gently dismisses Daniel, telling him that the words are locked and sealed until the end of the age. God did not intend to explain every detail before it occurred. Believers must wait patiently because the events themselves will make the meaning clear when the time arrives.

Suffering will serve as a refining fire to wash and purify believers, stripping away their sins and making them spiritually pure. Wicked people, on the other hand, will stay spiritually blind, refuse correction, and continue in their rebellion. Those who genuinely love God will receive wisdom from him to understand the purpose of their trials.

A period of 1,290 days is counted from the moment the daily temple sacrifice is halted and a sickening idolatrous statue is set up. This was fulfilled when the wicked Syrian king Antiochus Epiphanes stopped Jewish worship and profaned the temple altar. It reminded God's people that their worst persecutions have an exact expiration date set by God.

differ.view: This foretells a future Antichrist halting sacrifices in a rebuilt Jerusalem temple during the Great Tribulation, followed by thirty days leading to judgment.
The end of sacrifices began when Christ completed all temple rituals on the cross, followed by the Roman armies bringing idolatrous standards to destroy the temple in AD 70.

notes.meaning: The angel promises a special blessing to anyone who waits in faith for forty-five additional days, reaching 1,335 days. God frequently asks his servants to persevere past their initial expectations before the full dawn of deliverance arrives. Those who endure patiently through every delay will experience deep peace and lasting joy.

Daniel is told to go about his life and be at peace, knowing that his earthly duties will soon draw to a close. He will die quietly and rest from his labors in the grave. At the final resurrection, he will rise again to claim his eternal share and inheritance in God's heavenly kingdom.
